# Curated cross-tool compositions

This guide contains only non-obvious focused-profile recipes whose limitations matter. It is not an exhaustive history of tool names or a promise that every hidden or retired capability has a faithful composition.

## Author a live artifact from scratch

A board or dashboard is a `Document` record with `kind:"artifact"`, authored
source in `body`, and a governed `runtime` facet. Create it through
`records_write.create_record`. `artifacts_write.instantiate_artifact` copies an
existing artifact; its required source is not evidence that new artifacts
cannot be authored. If discovery is incomplete, report what you have not
found rather than asserting that a capability is unsupported.

Use `schema_read.preview_record_shape` with `type:"Document", kind:"artifact"`
for current shape advice; include candidate `facets` to check runtime values.
For new record-backed layouts,
start with `native.html.v1`, and prefer it for anything a person is meant to
look at: its self-contained HTML renders as authored, and a
`native.html.artifact.v2` declaration carries the same typed `interactions`
entries as MDX v2, so a write surface is no longer a reason to prefer MDX
(`native.html.artifact.v1` remains read-only). Choose `native.mdx.v2` when the
artifact must sit inside Native's own chrome and match it, or when an agent
must point at part of the rendered view: it renders through host-owned
components, and `render_artifact` returns a typed plan whose typed regions
establish semantic placement, where HTML returns only an isolated launch
descriptor. `verify_artifact` serves both, differently: a bounded attested
screen/print matrix for HTML, one advisory canonical-screen observation for
MDX v2. HTML's isolated runtime has no module
imports, no host theming and no ambient network, so a consistent look across
many HTML artifacts is an authoring discipline rather than something the host
supplies. Existing
`native.board.v1` and `native.mdx.v1` artifacts have their own
contracts; do not assume they accept a v2 manifest. A runtime name alone does
not adapt a static file into a live view.

For HTML interactions, put `schema`, `inputs`, `capability_requests` and
`interactions` in the existing inert `native-artifact-manifest` JSON element.
Request `input.read` for each exposed port and bind/grant the exact source as
usual. There is no separate write-proposal grant. From authored JavaScript,
`await nativeArtifact.propose({request_id:"triage-1",entry_id:"mark_triaged",slots:{record:recordId},values:{}})`
proposes declared writes. A newer proposal supersedes an older one still
awaiting review; only a write already being applied cannot be torn down. The
host supplies artifact/source identity,
observed CAS versions and idempotency; none belong in the proposal or
authored input. Settlement is commit-on-gesture: a proposal made during the
terminal event of a completed gesture (`click`, `drop`) carries the frame's
gesture-backed mark — necessary but never sufficient, since the host
additionally requires its own `navigator.userActivation` — and only a
declared, in-scope, reversible write then commits with no Apply step. A
proposal made outside a gesture still reaches the host and routes to the
Apply tray rather than throwing; irreversible effects such as record
creation, and browsers without `userActivation`, likewise keep the Apply
step. Apply resolves the current declaration, bound input and authenticated
caller again through `artifacts_execute.invoke_artifact_interaction`.
A committed write leaves a host-owned settled-change trace with a real
reversal through an ordinary declared entry. Relation rows
remain read-only; writable record slots require Collection-envelope inputs.

Reversibility is resolved against the value the write replaced, so a
`facet.set` on a facet that can be absent also needs a `facet.unset` declared
on the same facet. Only `facet.unset` can assert an absent prior value, so
without one a write replacing an absent value is not reversible and routes to
the Apply tray even though the artifact and the gesture are both valid; the
prior is read per record, so this is per record rather than once overall.
Later writes commit on the gesture when a declared `facet.set` can assert the
value they replace — for a toggle-shaped facet, a tray that appears only the
first time, but a facet holding a value from outside the declaration keeps
traying until it holds a covered one. A declared facet value must be a
string, number or object (booleans are refused; carry `"true"`/`"false"` as
strings), and `facet.unset` declares no value and no value slot.

For an ongoing Native view, bind canonical inputs and let the host re-resolve
them under the current viewer's authority; do not paste current records or
edges into the artifact body. Omit `as_of` for that live path. Use copied data
or a historical boundary only when the person intentionally asks for a
snapshot, and label what it captures. Check that the runtime and every input
support replay before using `as_of`; historical governed-SQL relation execution
is not supported.

The following minimal MDX v2 example presents names from an existing governed
Collection. Replace placeholders with returned identities. Call `bootstrap`
once and carry its `run_key` on each executor envelope. The operation and its
nested `arguments` are separate fields; `describe_operation` gives the current
contract when needed.

1. Call `records_write` with `operation:"create_record"` and these arguments,
   setting `body` to the complete MDX source below:

   ```json
   {"type":"Document","kind":"artifact","name":"Live items","facets":{"runtime":"native.mdx.v2"},"body":"<MDX source below>","reason":"Present the existing Collection without copying its records into a static view."}
   ```

   ```mdx
   export const nativeArtifact = {
     schema: "native.mdx.artifact.v2",
     inputs: {
       items: {
         envelope: "native.collection-envelope.v1",
         required: true,
         expose_to_root: true
       }
     },
     module_inputs: {},
     capability_requests: [
       { capability: "input.read", scope: { port: "items" } }
     ]
   }

   # Live items

   {native.inputs.items.records.length
     ? <ul>{native.inputs.items.records.map(item => <li>{item.name}</li>)}</ul>
     : <p>No visible items.</p>}
   ```

2. Bind the declared port through `artifacts_write`, operation
   `manage_artifact_inputs.bind`:

   ```json
   {"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","port_name":"items","collection_id":"<Collection ID>"}
   ```

3. Inspect the exact source through `access_read`, operation
   `manage_artifact_module_grants.read`, with `{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>"}`.
   Use the returned artifact-source subject's event identity and source digest
   in the next step; do not invent them or copy a module-release subject.

4. Prepare `access_admin`, operation `manage_artifact_module_grants.grant`:

   ```json
   {"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_kind":"artifact_source","subject_record_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_event_id":"<source event ID>","source_sha256":"<source digest>","capability":"input.read","scope":{"artifact_port":"items"}}
   ```

   Preparation does not grant anything. Review the returned target and effect
   within the person's authorization, then execute with the same operation,
   `plan_id`, `target` and `effect_summary` returned by preparation, without
   nested arguments. A manifest declares `scope.port`; this root-source grant
   uses `scope.artifact_port`. Grants authorize the declared runtime request;
   they do not confer visibility of otherwise unreadable records. Adding
   `RecordCard` or `RecordTable` also requires the declared and granted
   `navigation.record.user_gesture` capability with an empty scope.

5. Call `artifacts_execute.render_artifact` with `{"id":"<artifact ID>"}`.
   A diagnostic is not a successful render. Inspect the returned plan and
   provenance. For painted appearance, use `artifacts_read.verify_artifact`
   when available; report a missing verifier rather than claiming pixels were
   checked.

A later body edit carries each port's binding and grant forward unless that
port's own declaration changed or the manifest withdrew the matching capability
request, so adding a port drops nothing and a port-less grant such as
`navigation.record.user_gesture` survives while its request stands; whatever
does drop is named in the write receipt's `artifact_input_continuity.dropped`.

The body consumes `native.inputs.items.records`; binding alone does not make
hard-coded cards live. Later renders re-resolve the bound Collection under the
opener's authority, and an already-open MDX v2 view follows the host's live
refresh stream. Verify fresh resolution by changing an authorized source record
and rendering again without rewriting the artifact body. That smoke check does
not itself prove how an already-open tab refreshes. Keep query limits and any
incomplete cohort visible. A relation input instead uses its declared schema
and `.relation.rows`; it is not interchangeable with `.records`.

A kanban can group these input records by a facet present in that Collection,
retaining empty stages and handling missing or unexpected values explicitly.
Inspect the actual envelope and governed facet values before choosing the
grouping expression. Keep the source records authoritative.

MDX v2 is a constrained authoring language, not an arbitrary React module.
Start with the manifest export and Markdown/JSX; put filtering and mapping
inside JSX expressions rather than bare top-level `const` statements. Do not
add React `key`, inline `style`, `<style>` elements, `className`, event-handler
props or DOM APIs.
Use host layout components: `Grid` accepts `columns` and `gap`, each an integer
from 1 through 4. For example, keep the `items` manifest above and replace its
heading/list with this body (substitute the Collection's actual stage values):

```mdx
<Grid columns={3} gap={2}>
  {["backlog", "active", "done"].map(stage => <section>
    <h2>{stage}</h2>
    <ul>{native.inputs.items.records.filter(record => record.facets.stage === stage).map(record => <li>{record.name}</li>)}</ul>
  </section>)}
</Grid>
```

Every declared stage has a heading even when empty. Add an explicit group for
missing or unrecognized stage values when the Collection permits them. Render
the smallest source first, then add presentation features and re-render after
each change, including binding changes. A render from before the final write
does not verify the final artifact.

### Fields outside the nine fixed record fields

The record row carries nine fixed fields: `id`, `type`, `kind`, `name`,
`summary`, `lifecycle_interpretation`, `maturity`, `persistence`, and `facets`.
The shape stays closed — there is no wider row to request. For anything else —
aggregates, joins, derived values — use a governed SQL relation port: save the
computation as a `governed_sql` query Collection, declare a
`native.relation-envelope.v1` port carrying its `schema_sha256` and relation
dependencies, and bind that Collection. Rendering reruns the saved query under
the viewer's authority and delivers authorization-filtered rows beside the
record grain; `native.html.v1` accepts the port. Do not mirror derived values
into record facets to smuggle them through the record grain. The relationship
map below and the comment-count aggregate after it are two instances of this
rule: one draws edges, the other counts per record.

### Minimal HTML relationship map

HTML suits this map: the artifact draws the graph itself, while the data stays
in governed inputs. This complete document expects a `nodes` Collection and an
`edges` governed-SQL query Collection. The edge query must select only the
intended cohort from `links`, declare these output columns in this order, and
use `row_identity:["id"]` with a final `id` order key:

```json
[
  {"name":"id","type":"identifier","nullable":false},
  {"name":"source_id","type":"identifier","nullable":false},
  {"name":"target_id","type":"identifier","nullable":false},
  {"name":"relationship","type":"text","nullable":false}
]
```

Its `schema_sha256` is
`83a19095d4d5dea8e6bcd44a29a7abfb3914dfbec8134672079c15d831aeacbf`,
and its exact semantic dependency is
`links` → `native.query-sql.links` version 1. Read `engine_info` for the active
profile and catalog revisions when creating the saved query; do not copy those
values from an example. Restrict both endpoints in SQL. Filtering again in the
document prevents cross-scope lines from being painted, but cannot recover a
relevant edge omitted by an over-broad bounded query.

Write the document's scripts as plain JavaScript with JSDoc type annotations
on functions and non-obvious values (strongly recommended, not required):
your source is never transpiled, and its own bytes are what `body_digest`
covers, so JSDoc keeps most of the rigour with no runtime transform and no
change to the digest model. (The delivered document is your source
untransformed plus the host's injected bootstrap script — not byte-identical
to what you wrote, but never rewritten.) TypeScript syntax does not work here:
no transform runs over the body, so annotations would reach the browser as-is
and fail at parse. Every identifier a script references must be defined in the
document, be a browser global, or be the runtime bridge: there are no imports
and no external scripts (the CSP forbids both, and `eval`). Declare the bridge
and the named input port shapes with `@typedef`, so later type checking has
something to check against. For example, against the `nodes`/`edges` ports of
the document below:

```js
/**
 * Bridge the host injects before authored scripts run.
 * @typedef {object} NativeArtifactBridge
 * @property {Promise<{input: ArtifactInputEnvelope}>} ready - resolves with the first delivery object.
 * @property {function(function({input: ArtifactInputEnvelope}): void): function(): void} onInput - repaint on refresh; returns an unsubscribe function.
 */

/** @typedef {object} ArtifactInputEnvelope
 * @property {string} version
 * @property {string} mode
 * @property {ArtifactInputs} inputs
 */

/** @typedef {object} ArtifactInputs
 * @property {{records: NodeRecord[]}} nodes
 * @property {{relation: {rows: EdgeRow[]}}} edges
 */

/** @typedef {object} NodeRecord
 * @property {string} id
 * @property {string} name
 */

/** @typedef {object} EdgeRow
 * @property {string} id
 * @property {string} source_id
 * @property {string} target_id
 * @property {string} relationship
 */

/**
 * The host guarantees this global before authored scripts run; the cast only
 * tells the checker its shape. Never redeclare it with
 * `var nativeArtifact = ...`: that assigns to a non-writable global, which
 * silently no-ops in sloppy mode and throws under "use strict".
 * @type {NativeArtifactBridge}
 */
var bridge = /** @type {any} */ (window).nativeArtifact;

/**
 * Count edges with both endpoints visible.
 * @param {NodeRecord[]} nodes
 * @param {EdgeRow[]} rows
 * @returns {number}
 */
function countVisibleEdges(nodes, rows) {
  var ids = new Set(nodes.map(function (node) { return node.id; }));
  return rows.filter(function (edge) {
    return ids.has(edge.source_id) && ids.has(edge.target_id);
  }).length;
}

/**
 * Write the status line; the element is defined by the document below.
 * @param {string} text
 * @returns {void}
 */
function setStatus(text) {
  var statusNode = document.querySelector("#status");
  if (statusNode === null) {
    return;
  }
  statusNode.textContent = text;
}

/**
 * Paint one delivery: the port map lives at `delivery.input.inputs`.
 * @param {{input: ArtifactInputEnvelope}} delivery
 * @returns {void}
 */
function paint(delivery) {
  var inputs = delivery.input.inputs;
  var visible = countVisibleEdges(inputs.nodes.records, inputs.edges.relation.rows);
  setStatus(visible + " visible relationships.");
}

bridge.onInput(paint);
bridge.ready.then(paint).catch(function () {
  setStatus("Inputs unavailable.");
});
```

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Relationship map</title>
  <script type="application/json" id="native-artifact-manifest">{
    "schema":"native.html.artifact.v1",
    "inputs":{
      "nodes":{"envelope":"native.collection-envelope.v1","required":true,"expose_to_root":true},
      "edges":{
        "envelope":"native.relation-envelope.v1","required":true,"expose_to_root":true,
        "schema_sha256":"83a19095d4d5dea8e6bcd44a29a7abfb3914dfbec8134672079c15d831aeacbf",
        "relations":{"links":{"identity":"native.query-sql.links","semantic_version":1}}
      }
    },
    "capability_requests":[
      {"capability":"input.read","scope":{"port":"nodes"}},
      {"capability":"input.read","scope":{"port":"edges"}}
    ]
  }</script>
  <style>
    body { margin: 0; font: 15px system-ui, sans-serif; color: #172033; background: #f6f3ec; }
    main { max-width: 760px; margin: auto; padding: 24px; }
    svg { width: 100%; min-height: 180px; background: white; border: 1px solid #d7d2c7; }
    line { stroke: #8a91a0; stroke-width: 2; }
    circle { fill: #e4ecff; stroke: #4969a8; }
    text { text-anchor: middle; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<main>
  <h1>Relationship map</h1>
  <p id="status" role="status">Waiting for governed inputs…</p>
  <svg aria-label="Relationship map"></svg>
</main>
<script>
  var svg = document.querySelector("svg");
  var statusNode = document.querySelector("#status");
  var ns = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  function paint(delivery) {
    var inputs = delivery && delivery.input && delivery.input.inputs;
    var nodes = inputs && inputs.nodes && inputs.nodes.records;
    var relation = inputs && inputs.edges && inputs.edges.relation;
    var rows = relation && relation.rows;
    if (!Array.isArray(nodes) || !Array.isArray(rows)) {
      statusNode.textContent = "Inputs unavailable.";
      return;
    }

    svg.replaceChildren();
    var partial = relation.extent && relation.extent.complete !== true;
    var bestEffort = relation.extent &&
      relation.extent.source_completeness === "best_effort";
    if (!nodes.length) {
      statusNode.textContent = "No visible nodes" +
        (partial ? "; edge result is partial" : "") +
        (bestEffort ? "; edge source is best effort" : "") + ".";
      return;
    }

    var positions = new Map();
    nodes.forEach(function (node, index) {
      positions.set(node.id, {x: 90 + (index % 4) * 180, y: 60 + Math.floor(index / 4) * 100});
    });
    var height = 120 + Math.floor((nodes.length - 1) / 4) * 100;
    svg.setAttribute("viewBox", "0 0 720 " + height);

    var visibleEdges = rows.filter(function (edge) {
      return positions.has(edge.source_id) && positions.has(edge.target_id);
    });
    visibleEdges.forEach(function (edge) {
      var from = positions.get(edge.source_id);
      var to = positions.get(edge.target_id);
      var line = document.createElementNS(ns, "line");
      line.setAttribute("x1", from.x); line.setAttribute("y1", from.y);
      line.setAttribute("x2", to.x); line.setAttribute("y2", to.y);
      var title = document.createElementNS(ns, "title");
      title.textContent = edge.relationship;
      line.appendChild(title); svg.appendChild(line);
    });
    nodes.forEach(function (node) {
      var point = positions.get(node.id);
      var circle = document.createElementNS(ns, "circle");
      circle.setAttribute("cx", point.x); circle.setAttribute("cy", point.y);
      circle.setAttribute("r", 28); svg.appendChild(circle);
      var label = document.createElementNS(ns, "text");
      label.setAttribute("x", point.x); label.setAttribute("y", point.y + 48);
      label.textContent = node.name; svg.appendChild(label);
    });

    var outside = rows.length - visibleEdges.length;
    statusNode.textContent = nodes.length + " nodes; " + visibleEdges.length +
      " relationships" + (outside ? "; " + outside + " outside node scope" : "") +
      (partial ? "; partial edge result" : "") +
      (bestEffort ? "; edge source is best effort" : "") + ".";
  }

  window.nativeArtifact.onInput(paint);
  window.nativeArtifact.ready.then(paint).catch(function () {
    statusNode.textContent = "Inputs unavailable.";
  });
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

Create the artifact as in step 1 with `runtime:"native.html.v1"` and this
document as its complete `body`. Bind both ports with
`manage_artifact_inputs.bind`:

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","port_name":"nodes","collection_id":"<node Collection ID>"}
```

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","port_name":"edges","collection_id":"<governed edge-query Collection ID>"}
```

Read the current artifact-source identity as in step 3, then prepare and execute
one exact-source grant per port as in step 4, changing only
`scope.artifact_port` between `nodes` and `edges`:

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_kind":"artifact_source","subject_record_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_event_id":"<source event ID>","source_sha256":"<source digest>","capability":"input.read","scope":{"artifact_port":"nodes"}}
```

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_kind":"artifact_source","subject_record_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_event_id":"<source event ID>","source_sha256":"<source digest>","capability":"input.read","scope":{"artifact_port":"edges"}}
```

The node binding defines scope; its current caller-visible resolution defines
membership. The edge query has its own cohort scope and row bound, so keep both
aligned as node membership changes. Refresh re-runs that query; it does not
discover new relevant entities or rewrite the query's cohort. A valid empty
array means the current viewer sees no matching nodes or edges. A missing
binding, grant, required input, or compatible query makes the render unavailable
before document code runs. `extent.complete:false` means the returned edge
result is partial; `extent.source_completeness:"best_effort"` separately means
the source observation was best effort. The document labels both.

The host re-resolves both ports in one snapshot on each live refresh. Registering
`onInput` lets the same frame repaint when its input digest changes; `ready`
paints the initial delivery. Without an input subscriber, changed input still
stays live by relaunching the frame, but frame-local JavaScript state is lost.

### Comment counts per record

The same port answers "a count on each row", the case the closed row cannot
express. A comment is an `Annotation` record of kind `comment`, and its
`part_of` link points at its record for a root comment but at the root comment
for a reply, so counting links to the record alone would silently omit every
reply. The statement below counts both — each root through the record, each
reply through its root — with two ordinary joins and `COUNT(DISTINCT …)`, never
a per-row subquery, so it stays inside the query deadline. A governed comment is
itself a record, so the `WHERE` clause excludes comment rows: every returned row
is a non-comment record and `comment_count` means the same thing throughout.
Declare these output columns in this order, with `row_identity:["id"]` and a
final `id` order key:

```json
[
  {"name":"id","type":"identifier","nullable":false},
  {"name":"name","type":"text","nullable":false},
  {"name":"comment_count","type":"integer","nullable":false}
]
```

Its `schema_sha256` is
`ad03fda0c28b28adfc455e456a7cb0f319d9530a4be386ed04b6c1f57d5da8b1`,
and its exact semantic dependencies are
`records` → `native.query-sql.records` version 1 and
`links` → `native.query-sql.links` version 1. Read `engine_info` for the active
profile and catalog revisions when creating the saved query; do not copy those
values from an example. The statement joins the record to its root comments,
then each root comment to its replies, and counts both within one home;
`comment_count` is zero for a record with none:

```sql
SELECT r.id AS id, r.name AS name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT root_comment.id) + COUNT(DISTINCT reply.id) AS comment_count
FROM records r
LEFT JOIN links root_link
  ON root_link.target_id = r.id AND root_link.relationship = 'part_of'
LEFT JOIN records root_comment
  ON root_comment.id = root_link.source_id
 AND root_comment.type = 'Annotation' AND root_comment.kind = 'comment'
LEFT JOIN links reply_link
  ON reply_link.target_id = root_comment.id AND reply_link.relationship = 'part_of'
LEFT JOIN records reply
  ON reply.id = reply_link.source_id
 AND reply.type = 'Annotation' AND reply.kind = 'comment'
WHERE r.home_id = ?1
  AND (r.type <> 'Annotation' OR r.kind IS NULL OR r.kind <> 'comment')
GROUP BY r.id, r.name
ORDER BY r.name ASC, r.id ASC
```

Scope the aggregate to the same cohort as the bound `items` collection — here,
its home, passed as `?1` with
`"parameters":[{"type":"text","value":"<home folder id>"}]` — because an
unscoped aggregate returns a row for every visible record, exceeds the row
bound, and silently truncates, leaving the artifact's own rows uncounted rather
than visibly wrong.

Declare the aggregate beside the record grain, bind the saved-query Collection
to it, and grant it exactly as in the map above — one
`manage_artifact_inputs.bind` per port and one exact-source `input.read` grant
per port:

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","port_name":"items","collection_id":"<record Collection ID>"}
```

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","port_name":"comment_counts","collection_id":"<query Collection ID>"}
```

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_kind":"artifact_source","subject_record_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_event_id":"<source event ID>","source_sha256":"<source digest>","capability":"input.read","scope":{"artifact_port":"items"}}
```

```json
{"artifact_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_kind":"artifact_source","subject_record_id":"<artifact ID>","subject_event_id":"<source event ID>","source_sha256":"<source digest>","capability":"input.read","scope":{"artifact_port":"comment_counts"}}
```

with this port beside the record grain in the manifest:

```json
"comment_counts": {"envelope": "native.relation-envelope.v1", "required": true, "expose_to_root": true, "schema_sha256": "ad03fda0c28b28adfc455e456a7cb0f319d9530a4be386ed04b6c1f57d5da8b1", "relations": {"records": {"identity": "native.query-sql.records", "semantic_version": 1}, "links": {"identity": "native.query-sql.links", "semantic_version": 1}}}
```

The document joins each count to its record by `id` from the same delivery
shape the map reads — `delivery.input.inputs` — wired to `onInput` and `ready`
the same way:

```js
function paintCounts(delivery) {
  var inputs = delivery && delivery.input && delivery.input.inputs;
  var relation = inputs && inputs.comment_counts && inputs.comment_counts.relation;
  var rows = relation && relation.rows;
  if (!Array.isArray(rows)) return;
  var counts = new Map(rows.map(function (row) { return [row.id, row.comment_count]; }));
  var partial = relation.extent && relation.extent.complete !== true;
  var bestEffort = relation.extent &&
    relation.extent.source_completeness === "best_effort";
  // ...render each record with counts.get(record.id), labelling partial/bestEffort
}
```

`extent.complete:false` means the returned count result is partial and its
`total` is null — it never claims a known total.
`extent.source_completeness:"best_effort"` separately means the source
observation was best effort. Saving validates the same contract execution
rechecks: declared relations must match the relations the statement reads,
output columns must match the statement labels, the digest must match the
columns, and the final order key must be the one non-null identifier.

## Attention and dashboard view with bounded queries

Build an attention view with bounded, valid `query_record` calls:

1. Query the installation's known active lifecycle tokens, for example `{"steps":[{"step":"filter","types":["WorkItem"],"lifecycle":["active","claimed"]}],"order":"last_activity_desc","limit":50}`. Lifecycle is open, so the caller must supply the tokens that mean active locally.
2. Find stale candidates by paging the same scope with `order:"last_activity_desc"`, a bounded `limit`, and increasing `offset`. Compare each returned `last_activity_at` with the cutoff client-side. `query_record` has inclusive `last_activity_since` but no before predicate, so the stale set is incomplete until paging reaches the cutoff or exhausts the match set; disclose any earlier stop. For the built-in faithful bounded view, call the hidden-by-profile `get_dashboard` by exact name with `stale_after_days`.
3. From a bounded work-ID seed, traverse outgoing dependencies with `{"steps":[{"step":"filter","ids":["work-id"]},{"step":"traverse","target":"links","relationship":"depends_on","direction":"out"}],"limit":50}`. Run a separate traversal for `blocks` or the reverse direction when the installation uses that edge convention; each traversal replaces the working set.
4. Request the lifecycle census with `{"steps":[{"step":"filter","types":["WorkItem"]}],"count_by":"lifecycle"}`. Keep the filter aligned with the visible dashboard scope.

Keep scope and `include_archived` policy identical across calls and report each window's limits. These calls are **not one atomic snapshot**: writes may land between them, so rows and buckets can describe slightly different revisions. A shared supported `as_of` boundary pins content for each `query_record` call, but schema and governed-kind metadata remain live; otherwise disclose the skew.

## Governed facet selection

First call `resolve_facets` for the exact record or type/kind context. Read the effective facet shape and the governing vocabulary identity from the resolved pack → user cascade. Then call `manage_vocabularies` with `action:"list_values"`, that vocabulary, `status:"active"`, and `resolve_aliases:true`. Write the selected canonical value through `create_record` or `update_record` with its vocabulary reference.

Do not skip resolution and guess a vocabulary by name. The cascade can change which vocabulary governs the same facet key, and aliases or deprecated values can make an apparently plausible token wrong. The write path will enforce the effective contract, but resolving first avoids a preventable failed or misdirected choice.

## Semantic bulk operations

Use a bulk operation only when it supplies semantics beyond scheduling the same call repeatedly:

- `records_read.resolve_many` resolves a bounded, ordered list of exact names and reports unique, absent, and ambiguous outcomes without exposing hidden candidates. Use it for deterministic deduplication; use `search` for exploratory lexical recall.
- `records_write.create_many` creates a bounded graph. Batch-local `ref` values can be used by `parent_ref`, link `target_ref`, and `[[ref]]` body mentions. The server validates the whole dependency graph before writing, then returns positional receipts; one failed record prevents its dependants but not independent branches.
- `access_admin.manage_record_policy.set_many` converges each `(record, subject)` pair on an exact capability or on absence. It is one plan-required, all-or-nothing effect: prepare it first, review the complete target/effect summary, and execute only that returned plan.

For independent ordinary calls with no shared lookup, graph, or convergence semantics, pipeline the singular operations instead. A generic heterogeneous batch does not reduce response payload and does not provide cross-operation atomicity. Prefer compact response/receipt modes when payload size is the actual cost.
